title: wall-scan output
description: Discovers devices on IPv4 networks using nmap. Usage: wall-scan TARGET [TARGET ...] [--ports LIST | --no-ports] [--privileged]. Prints exactly one document to stdout. Lists only the hosts that responded, and how each scanned network is reached (schema 1.1).

status.description: ok: finished with no errors. partial: finished, result present but incomplete (see errors). error: failed, result is null.

result.description: Tool-specific payload; null when status is error.

allOf.$comment: partial -> at least one error, result present
error -> at least one error, result is null

schema_version.description: Contract version, MAJOR.MINOR. This file is the contract for major version 1: every 1.x document must validate against it.

name.description: Program that produced the document, e.g. "wall-scan".

version.description: Package version of that program (its git tag without the leading v). Independent of schema_version.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time in UTC with a Z suffix, e.g. "2026-10-08T09:30:00Z". Fractional seconds allowed.

code.description: Machine-readable snake_case code. Open set: new codes may appear in any minor version, so consumers must handle codes they do not know.

message.description: Human-readable explanation, safe to show in the UI.

target.description: The input (usually an IP address) this error is about, or null for an error affecting the whole run.

params.description: The inputs of this run, echoed back so a stored result describes itself.

targets.description: IPv4 addresses and/or CIDR ranges, as given on the command line.

ports.description: Port list passed to nmap -p, e.g. "22,80,443,445,3389,9100" or "1-1024". null means discovery only (nmap -sn): no ports were scanned and every device's open_ports is null.

privileged.description: Whether nmap ran with raw-socket privileges (--privileged, or running as root). Without them nmap cannot use ARP, so mac and vendor are null for every device.

timeout_s.description: Time limit for the whole scan in seconds. nmap is stopped when it is reached, and the run fails with error code scan_timeout.

engine.description: The scanner that did the work: nmap and its version for the Python tool. A reimplementation reports its own name and version here.

hosts_scanned.description: Number of addresses probed (nmap: runstats/hosts/@total). Addresses that did not respond are not listed in devices.

devices.description: Hosts that responded, sorted by IP address (numerically, so .9 comes before .10).

networks.description: Added in schema 1.1, so absent from 1.0 documents. How the scanning host reaches each scanned range, from its routing table: one entry per range in params.targets (prefix /30 or shorter), in the same order. Single addresses have no entry.

network.description: The range, exactly as in params.targets.

attached.description: true: the scanning host is directly on this network (no router in between, so MAC addresses are visible). false: it is reached through a router, or there is no route to it. null: the routing table could not be read (it is read on Linux only).

interface.description: The scanning host's network interface the traffic leaves on, e.g. eth0. null when the routing table could not be read or has no route to the network.

address.description: The scanning host's own address in this network, as chosen by the operating system. null when it has no address in it (the network is reached through a router).

gateway.description: The router of this network as the scanning host sees it. For an attached network: the gateway of a default route out of the same interface, if that gateway is inside the network. For a network reached through a router: that router (the next hop). null when there is none or it is not known.

mac.description: Lowercase and colon-separated. null when unknown: unprivileged scan, host on another subnet (MAC addresses do not cross routers), or the scanning host itself.

vendor.description: Manufacturer looked up from the MAC prefix (OUI). null when mac is null or the prefix is unknown, which includes the randomised MAC addresses used by phones and laptops.

hostname.description: Name from reverse DNS (PTR record). null when there is none.

discovery_reason.description: Why the host counted as up, as reported by nmap (status/@reason), e.g. arp-response, echo-reply, syn-ack, localhost-response.

open_ports.description: Ports in state open, sorted by protocol then port. [] = ports were scanned and none is open. null = ports were not scanned (params.ports is null).

service.description: nmap service name, e.g. ssh, http, ipp, jetdirect. Without version detection (-sV) this is a guess from the port number. null if nmap has no name for the port.
